0|02092a2f034fdeabab524ae39c2de86ba9ffa15a|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"xfs: Check for extent overflow when renaming dir entries
A rename operation is essentially a directory entry remove operation
from the perspective of parent directory (i.e. src_dp) of rename's
source. Hence the only place where we check for extent count overflow
for src_dp is in xfs_bmap_del_extent_real(). xfs_bmap_del_extent_real()
returns -ENOSPC when it detects a possible extent count overflow and in
response
column2: the higher layers of directory handling code do the following:

column1: 1. Data/Free blocks: XFS lets these blocks linger until a future remove
operation removes them.
2. Dabtree blocks: XFS swaps the blocks with the last block in the Leaf
space and unmaps the last block.
For target_dp
column2: there are two cases depending on whether the destination

column1: directory entry exists or not.
When destination directory entry does not exist (i.e. target_ip ==
NULL)
column2: extent count overflow check is performed only when transaction

column1: has a non-zero sized space reservation associated with it.  With a
zero-sized space reservation
column2: XFS allows a rename operation to continue

column1: only when the directory has sufficient free space in its data/leaf/free
space blocks to hold the new entry.
When destination directory entry exists (i.e. target_ip != NULL)
we need to do is change the inode number associated with the already
existing entry. Hence there is no need to perform an extent count
overflow check.
